FDA Bhawan, Kotla Road,

New Delhi,

Date: ;

[4 JUN 2627

To
All State/UT Drugs Controllers,
Sub: Prescribing Information Leaflet change for “Mannitol” marketed in the
country- Reg.
Sir,
The National Co-ordination Centre for Pharmacovigilance Programme of India (NCC-
PvPl), functioning at IPC, Ghaziabad has forwarded their recommendation based on
ADR reports on Mannitol which was discussed by them in the 5" Signal Review
Panel (SRP) under the programme meeting held on og May, 2015 with an objective
to detect Signal/Prescribing Information Leaflet change from Indian database and
promote patient safety.
In the meeting, PvPI has evaluated the reported ADRs for Mannitol on the basis of
Individual Case Study Reports (ICSRs) and recommended CDSCO to take
necessary steps to incorporate Hypokalaemia as an adverse drug reaction in the
Prescribing Information Leaflet (PIL) of Mannitol marketed in the country.
Subsequently, PvPl recommendations was deliberated in the Subject Expert
Committee (SEC-Cardiovascular & Renal) meeting held on 19.05.2022 at CDSCO
(HQ), New Delhi.

After detailed deliberation, the committee recommended that CDSCO should
request the State Drugs Controllers to direct the manufacturers of the drug to include
Mannitol induced Hypokalaemia as an adverse drug reaction in the package insert
of the drug as suggested by PvPI.
The recommendation of the SEC has been considered by this office.
Accordingly, you are requested to direct the manufacturers of Mannitol under your
jurisdiction to incorporate Mannitol induced Hypokalaemia as an adverse drug
reaction in the package insert/promotional literature of the drug.
Action taken in this regard may be intimated to this office.
Yours faithfully,
Yee
~
Dr. V.G. Somani
Drugs Controller General (India)
